outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the uniform conjecture (finitely many coprime solutions of a^m + b^n = c^k over all exponent triples with 1/m + 1/n + 1/k < 1) has not been settled as far as my searches show: no source claims a proof and no new primitive solution has been reported, so the known list of ten solutions stands. Restricted cases did move: a bounded computer census for the classical equation (Sikora, Oct 2024); two unrefereed, IUT-based preprints claiming no solutions for all exponents at least 20 and for all signatures outside a listed exception set (Zhou, Mar and Oct 2025); a claimed cyclotomic proof for the exponent families (p,p,q) with p > 3 prime and q an odd prime distinct from p (Mihailescu, Sep 2025, with a coprimality gap in the extracted statement); a computer-assisted proof that x^3 + y^5 = z^7 has no coprime solutions, i.e. one signature settled (Chocian, 22 Sep 2026, with OpenAI Codex, OpenAI ChatGPT and Anthropic Claude credited in the paper).
problem_asks: (1) Uniform finiteness over exponents: the set of solutions, counted as distinct triples (a^m, b^n, c^k), with a, b, c positive coprime integers and m, n, k positive integers satisfying 1/m + 1/n + 1/k < 1, is finite. The claim covers all such exponent triples at once, not each triple separately. (2) Coprimality is a hypothesis. Wikipedia's wording and the survey's gcd(x, y, z) = 1 both give the gcd reading; pairwise coprimality would be a stronger reading. Not decided here; the judging pass should note it. (3) Finiteness only: the bullet asks for no complete list, no effective bound, and no claim that the ten known solutions are all of them. (4) All coefficients are 1. The analogue with arbitrary coefficients (A x^m + B y^n = C z^k, the survey's Conjecture 1.9) is a different question. (5) Positive integers only.

events.what_happened: Adam S. Sikora, 'Fermat-Catalan and Tijdeman-Zagier conjectures for products', arXiv:2410.21552 (single version). Proposes product-based generalisations and an explicit abc variant. Section 2 reports a computer verification for the classical equation: the listed coprime solutions are the only ones when min(n, m, k) <= 113 and all powers x^n, y^m, z^k are below M_min, with M_2 = 2^71, M_3 = 2^80, M_4 = 2^100, and M_d = 2^113 for 5 <= d <= 113. Remark 6 gives 5 <= d <= 21 for the product conjectures. Section 6 checks the product conjecture for a, b, c < 2^63 using ABC@Home data.
events.revisions: v1 only (28 Oct 2024) on the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: A bounded census for the classical equation, not a finiteness result: within min(m, n, k) <= 113 and the stated power bounds, the only coprime solutions are the known list of ten. The product-conjecture checks are not the Fermat-Catalan statement.
events.remains: Finiteness for all exponent triples. Not covered: solutions with min(m, n, k) >= 114, and solutions with powers beyond the stated bounds, for every exponent triple.
events.directly_checkable: The ten listed solutions can be checked by hand (for example 2^5 + 7^2 = 3^4). The search code and logs are not described as released in the text I read.
events.doubts: The search ran on cluster computers at the University at Buffalo (acknowledgement); no software is named and no code or logs were found. The stated range is inconsistent within the paper: 5 <= d <= 113 in Section 2, 5 <= d <= 21 in Remark 6 (product conjectures). No independent rerun found. Internal check only.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: the bounded search finds no new solutions.

ai.disclosed_cost: Computation on the University at Buffalo Center for Computational Research cluster; no compute quantities stated.

events.what_happened: Zhong-Peng Zhou, 'The inter-universal Teichmuller theory and new Diophantine results over the rational numbers. I', arXiv:2503.14510 (single author; listed 8 Mar 2025; footnote says submitted for publication 11 Sep 2024). Applies IUT, with the mu6 version of Mochizuki-Fesenko-Hoshi-Minamide-Porowski and a rational-number modification, to effective abc inequalities and generalised Fermat equations. Corollary B3: for r, s, t >= 20, or (r, s, t) a permutation of (3, 3, n) with n >= 3, there is no triple of non-zero coprime integers with x^r + y^s = z^t. The abstract says computational verification is involved.
events.delivers: Claimed: for the coefficient-1 equation, no coprime solutions in exponent triples with all three exponents at least 20 (conditional on the IUT-based argument as the paper presents it). This removes the tail min(m, n, k) >= 20 from the Fermat-Catalan search space, as claimed.
events.remains: All exponent triples with min(m, n, k) <= 19, including infinite families with a small fixed exponent; the uniform finiteness statement is not reached.
events.doubts: (a) The argument is built on the IUT framework of Mochizuki et al. The 2018 Scholze-Stix analysis reported a gap at Corollary 3.12 of IUT III (as cited in the LANA report discussion; the 2018 document itself was not opened). The ZEN LANA interim report (announced 17 July 2026) localises a compatibility question at the Theorem 3.11 to Corollary 3.12 step and withholds judgement (per the ZEN announcement and secondary coverage; the PDF was not readable). Kirti Joshi's July 2026 comments dispute LANA's reading (secondary; not opened). No source I read establishes whether Zhou's argument passes through the disputed step. (b) The computations behind Corollary B3 are named in the abstract only; I did not find their scope in the text I read. (c) No journal acceptance or expert report found. (d) No affiliation shown on the arXiv pages I opened.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: asserts no coprime solutions in a tail of exponent space and produces no solution.

events.what_happened: Zhong-Peng Zhou, 'The inter-universal Teichmuller theory and new Diophantine results over rational numbers. II', arXiv:2510.05448 (single author, no affiliation shown; listed 6 Oct 2025). Theorem A: for every signature (r, s, t) outside a listed exception set, x^r + y^s = z^t has no non-trivial primitive solutions beyond the Catalan solution 1^n + 2^3 = 3^2 and nine non-Catalan solutions. Exception set as extracted from the HTML: (4,5,n), (4,7,n), (5,6,n) for 7 <= n <= 303; (2,3,n), (3,4,n), (3,8,n), (3,10,n) for 11 <= n <= 109 or n in {113, 121}; (3,5,n) for 7 <= n <= 3677; (3,7,n), (3,11,n) for 11 <= n <= 667; (3,m,n) for 13 <= m <= 17 and m < n <= 29; (2,m,n) for m >= 5 and n >= 7. Corollaries: 244 signatures up to permutation remain for exponents >= 4; 2446 for the Beal conjecture. The abstract page says it is an older version to be updated soon.
events.revisions: v1 only as found (6 Oct 2025); the abstract page says 'This is an older version of the paper, which will be updated soon.'
events.delivers: Claimed: for each signature outside the exception set, the primitive solution set of x^r + y^s = z^t is the known list (Catalan plus nine). Restricted to coefficient 1, to the listed exceptions, and to the IUT-based argument.
events.remains: Every signature on the exception set, which includes the infinite family (2, m, n) with m >= 5 and n >= 7 and the listed finite families (including (3,5,7), since (3,5,n) for 7 <= n <= 3677 is excepted). So the uniform finiteness question over all signatures is not reached.
events.doubts: Same IUT dependency as the March 2025 paper: the 2018 Scholze-Stix objection and the July 2026 LANA interim report (withholding judgement) bear on the framework; no source I read establishes whether this paper's argument passes through the disputed step. The author states the version is older and will be updated, so the claimed signature list may change. No refereeing or expert engagement found in 12 months.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on the signatures it covers; it asserts the known list there and produces no new solution.

events.what_happened: Preda Mihailescu, 'The strong Fermat-Catalan equation', arXiv:2509.18275 (single version, submitted 22 Sep 2025). Abstract: a cyclotomic proof that (x^p + y^p)/(x + y) = p^e z^q has no solutions in coprime integers x, y, z when p > 3 and q is a distinct odd prime (e in {0,1}). Theorem 1, as extracted from the HTML: the strong equation has no integer solutions; 'In particular, the Fermat-Catalan equation x^p + y^p = z^q has no solutions with distinct odd primes p, q and p > 3.'
events.revisions: v1 only per arXiv (22 Sep 2025). The PDF header reads 'Version 1.0 August 24, 2026'; the conflict is not explained.
events.delivers: Claimed: the classical equation x^p + y^p = z^q has no solutions for prime p > 3 and a distinct odd prime q, i.e. the exponent family (p, p, q). The extracted 'in particular' statement carries no coprimality hypothesis, but one is needed: 2^5 + 2^5 = 4^3 is a non-coprime solution with p = 5, q = 3. So the statement must be read with gcd(x, y, z) = 1.
events.remains: Every other exponent triple: families (p, p, 2) and (p, p, 3) are treated elsewhere (Darmon-Merel 1997), (p, q, r) with distinct exponents, the case p = 3, and non-prime exponents. Uniform finiteness is not reached.
events.doubts: (a) Single author; no journal, referee report, or expert check found. (b) Scope: a cyclotomic argument covering all (p, p, q) with p > 3 prime and q an odd prime is much broader than the family-by-family treatments in the literature I found (Darmon-Merel for q = 2, 3; Dahmen-Siksek for specific (5,5,7), (5,5,19), (7,7,5)). That makes the claim a major one and so a natural target for checking. (c) The extracted Theorem 1 omits coprimality (see delivers). (d) A 2023 lecture abstract by the same author, seen in a search excerpt and not opened, described completion of the proof as still ahead. (e) The date conflict above.
events.direction: Claimed to cut toward the conjecture's expected outcome (no coprime solutions) for the (p, p, q) family.

events.what_happened: Peter Chocian, 'The Primitive Generalized Fermat Equation x^3 + y^5 = z^7: A computer-assisted proof', arXiv:2609.26996 (math.NT, cross-listed math.AG; v1 posted 22 Sep 2026). Claims that x^3 + y^5 = z^7 has no solution in non-zero coprime integers (swapping x and y gives x^5 + y^3 = z^7). Builds on Dahmen-Siksek (signed local descent; elimination of three reducible cases) and Putz (reduction of the irreducible case to seven septic fields). The new work excludes six pure fields via a Fano resolvent and a genus-three plane quartic over Q(sqrt(-7)), and one exceptional field via modularity and conductor results of Pacetti-Villagra Torcomian, level lowering over Q(sqrt(5)), and a finite Hecke comparison at 29. Finite calculations are supplied as exact certificates, programs and logs, described as replayed on an independent machine. The abstract page carries the comment 'Substantial AI-assisted research and writing; see the statement in Section 8'.
events.delivers: Claimed: for the exponent triple (3, 5, 7) with coefficients 1 and coprime non-zero integers, no solutions. This settles that one signature completely (per the claim). Nothing about other exponent triples or the uniform statement.
events.remains: All other exponent triples, including the infinitely many with min(m, n, k) = 2 that the known list contains, and the uniform finiteness statement.

events.what_happened: Anthropic, 'Formalizing Fermat's Last Theorem' (blog post dated 4 Sep 2026 in the post itself). A Lean 4 computer-checked formalisation of Fermat's Last Theorem following Wiles's approach, in a simplified version from Darmon-Diamond-Taylor. The post reports about 13 million lines of Lean and about 29,500 intermediate theorems; work by Claude, 'largely autonomously', with dozens of Claude agents; occasional high-level instructions from Tianyi Peng; review by Kevin Buzzard; a Prove2Me platform; and a Claude Code-based multi-agent harness. The model is named only as 'a general-purpose internal research model roughly comparable to Claude Fable 5.1'. The post reports about six billion output tokens over a little under two weeks. Secondary coverage gives 30,300 theorems and about $300,000; not verified.
events.delivers: A computer-checked verification of the already-proven case x^n + y^n = z^n (n >= 3) of the Fermat-Catalan family, which is the subfamily (n, n, n). It delivers nothing new about the conjecture: Wiles (1995) already established the result. The post itself says 'what's novel here is the verification'.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The subfamily (n, n, n) was already settled, and nothing here reaches the other exponent triples.

checked_by.qualification: Named in the post as reviewer of the formalised proof; an established Lean and number-theory formalisation expert.
checked_by.what_they_did: Reviewed the proof, per the Anthropic post.

machine_checked.system: Lean (version not stated in the post as I read it)

events.doubts: The formalisation is a very large AI-generated artefact; the post and secondary coverage say it does not yet enter Mathlib. Secondary coverage says it is free of unproved placeholders (sorry); I did not confirm this from the post. This is a discounted event for the Fermat-Catalan problem, not a doubt about FLT.
events.direction: Confirms the known result on the (n, n, n) subfamily; cuts toward the conjecture's expected outcome there.

events.what_happened: Jineon Baek and Seewoo Lee, 'Formalizing Mason-Stothers Theorem and its Corollaries in Lean 4', arXiv:2408.15180 (v1 27 Aug 2024; v2 25 Sep 2025, 'Addressed the latest reviews'). Lean 4 formalisation of Snyder's elementary proof of Mason-Stothers and several consequences, including non-solvability of Fermat-Catalan-type equations in polynomials. The v2 abstract says the formalisation has been integrated into mathlib.
events.revisions: v1 27 Aug 2024; v2 25 Sep 2025 ('Addressed the latest reviews').
events.delivers: A polynomial (function-field) analogue only: no non-constant coprime polynomial solutions of the Fermat-Catalan-type equation under the paper's exponent hypotheses. Discarded as a different question: the integers are not touched.
events.remains: The integer conjecture entirely (problem_asks, all parts).

checked_by.what_they_did: Integrated the formalisation into mathlib, per the v2 abstract.

events.doubts: None specific. I read the abstract page only, not the body. The 'sorry_free' value is inferred from mathlib integration.
events.direction: Analogue: polynomial version consistent with the conjecture. Says nothing about the integer case.

events.what_happened: Ariel Pacetti and Lucas Villagra Torcomian, 'On the generalized Fermat equation of signature (5, p, 3)', arXiv:2512.17845 (v1 19 Dec 2025). Using hypergeometric motives within the modular method, they give an explicit ramification analysis at primes dividing 2qr, identify a general obstruction to the modular method ('ghost solutions'), and, assuming a standard large-image conjecture, prove that x^5 + y^p + z^3 = 0 has no non-trivial primitive solutions (a, b, c) with 3 does not divide c, for p a sufficiently large prime.
events.delivers: Conditional on a large-image conjecture: for the signature (5, p, 3) with p sufficiently large (no explicit bound given), no primitive solutions with 3 not dividing c. A one-parameter family of exponent triples, with a restriction on c.
events.remains: Solutions with 3 dividing c; all p below the unspecified bound; the large-image hypothesis; every other signature; the uniform question.
events.doubts: The result is conditional on a large-image conjecture, which is assumed, not proved. The obstruction the authors identify means the method fails in many instances. Read from the abstract page only.
events.direction: Conditional support for the conjecture on one signature family; no solution found.

events.what_happened: Satyabrat Sahoo, 'Effective Generalized Fermat equation of signature (2p, 2q, r) with odd narrow class number', arXiv:2509.21083 (v1 25 Sep 2025). For each fixed prime r >= 5, a condition on solutions of the S-unit equation over Q(zeta_r + zeta_r^-1) yields a constant V_r such that x^(2p) + y^(2q) = z^r has no non-trivial primitive integer solutions whenever p, q >= V_r. Elliptic curves over that field are shown modular for every prime r >= 2, which makes V_r effectively computable. A criterion on r is given when the narrow class number of that field is odd.
events.delivers: Conditional (on the S-unit condition the abstract refers to; the condition is not spelled out in the abstract) and asymptotic: for fixed r and all p, q at least V_r, no primitive solutions. The criterion on r applies only when the narrow class number is odd.
events.remains: Small p and q below V_r; primes r for which the criterion fails; the S-unit condition if not verified; every other signature; the uniform question.
events.doubts: Conditional on an S-unit condition; V_r is not given explicitly in the abstract. Read from the abstract only. A later preprint (arXiv 2605.20860, seen in a search excerpt) cites it.
events.direction: Conditional, asymptotic support for the conjecture on the signature family (2p, 2q, r).

events.what_happened: Somnath Jha and Satyabrat Sahoo, 'Asymptotic Fermat equation of signature (r, r, p) over totally real fields', arXiv:2502.09892 (v1 14 Feb 2025; v2 7 Jul 2025). Studies x^r + y^r = d z^p over totally real fields for primes r, p >= 5, with the modular method.
events.delivers: Discarded as a different question: other field, a coefficient d, and asymptotic solutions over totally real fields. Nothing about the rational problem.
events.remains: problem_asks, all parts (this is not a result on the statement).
events.doubts: Not opened. Details from a search excerpt of the abstract.

disputes.summary: Zhou's two 2025 IUT-based preprints (arXiv:2503.14510, 2510.05448) rest on the Mochizuki-Fesenko-Hoshi-Minamide-Porowski IUT framework. The 2018 Scholze-Stix objection and the ZEN LANA interim report of 17 July 2026 (which localises a compatibility question at the Theorem 3.11 to Corollary 3.12 step and withholds judgement) bear on that framework. Kirti Joshi's July 2026 comments dispute LANA's reading; Mochizuki maintains the theory is understood by experts. No source I read establishes whether Zhou's argument passes through the disputed step. The secondary coverage headline 'Lean confirms gap' is not supported by the ZEN announcement, which withholds judgement.

summary: Found: no proof of the uniform conjecture, no new primitive solution, and the known list of ten (Wikipedia, number.subwiki, MathWorld agree; the Wikipedia lead says 'ten solutions are known' as of 2024) stands. The Wikipedia article's last substantive status update I could see cites Sikora's 2024 computation, and its lead still calls the conjecture open. What did move is restricted cases, and each is a different question from the uniform statement. (1) Sikora (arXiv:2410.21552, 28 Oct 2024): a bounded census. Within min(m, n, k) <= 113 and the stated power bounds (2^71 for min 2, 2^80 for 3, 2^100 for 4, 2^113 for 5 to 113), the coprime solutions are exactly the known list. This is a finite check of a bounded region and does not move finiteness. The stated range is inconsistent within the paper (5 <= d <= 113 in Section 2; 5 <= d <= 21 in Remark 6 for the product conjectures), and no code was found. (2) Zhou (arXiv:2503.14510, 8 Mar 2025; arXiv:2510.05448, 6 Oct 2025): claims no coprime solutions when all exponents are at least 20, and, for signatures outside a listed exception set (which includes the infinite family (2, m, n), m >= 5, n >= 7, and (3,5,7)), only the known solutions. Both are single-author, unrefereed, and rest on contested IUT. If the argument holds, the uniform question reduces to exponents with minimal value at most 19 and most signatures are settled; if it does not, neither paper moves the problem. Searches found no referee report, journal acceptance, or expert verification. The second paper says it is an older version to be updated. (3) Mihailescu (arXiv:2509.18275, 22 Sep 2025): claims a cyclotomic proof that the classical equation x^p + y^p = z^q has no solutions for prime p > 3 and distinct odd prime q, i.e. the whole (p, p, q) family, which is much broader than the family-by-family treatments I found. The extracted statement omits coprimality, which is needed: 2^5 + 2^5 = 4^3 is a non-coprime solution with p = 5, q = 3. The PDF header date (24 Aug 2026) conflicts with arXiv's 22 Sep 2025, unexplained. No engagement found. (4) Chocian (arXiv:2609.26996, 22 Sep 2026): claims x^3 + y^5 = z^7 has no non-zero coprime solutions, settling that one signature. Zhou's exception list excludes (3,5,7), so this and Zhou are complementary. It is 19 days old and unrefereed. It builds on Dahmen-Siksek (partial descent), Putz (seven septic fields), Pacetti-Villagra Torcomian's modularity and conductor results, level lowering, and finite calculations. Whether the Pacetti-Villagra inputs are unconditional is not established: their own paper on (5, p, 3) assumes a large-image conjecture. The paper's Section 8 (as read through a model-summarised fetch) credits OpenAI Codex with use 'in developing and checking mathematical arguments', OpenAI ChatGPT with 'supported the research and writing', and Anthropic Claude with an 'independent auditor' role; it says the author originated the approach and that the AI reviews are not human peer review or proof-assistant formalisation. This is the one event in the window where an AI system is credited with mathematics bearing on this problem. Whether those credits are load-bearing is the judging pass's call. The Anthropic FLT formalisation (4 Sep 2026) uses an AI system, but it formalises an existing proof of the (n, n, n) subfamily already settled by Wiles; it is recorded as discounted. Baek-Lee (Aug 2024) is a polynomial analogue, and Sahoo (Sep 2025) and Pacetti-Villagra (Dec 2025) are conditional results on signature families; none of these names an AI system. Searches for AI results on this problem in trackers, benchmark pages, the AlphaEvolve paper, Tao's blog, Quanta and MathOverflow found nothing for the Fermat-Catalan problem itself. The AlphaEvolve repository's 67 problems could not be checked by title, so that negative is not established. A Beal-conjecture proof claim by Vega (2024, unrefereed, not opened) covers only the exponent-at-least-3 slice and is discarded as a different problem. Where a call was close: Sikora's census could be read as a strong finite verification or as nothing for finiteness (I take the second: the bound is finite, not the conjecture's quantity). Zhou's claims could be read as large restrictions (if IUT is sound) or as unverified (I record them as claims, not restrictions, in the events). Mihailescu's claim is recorded as stated, with the coprimality gap flagged.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a larger movement: take Zhou II's Theorem A at face value, and Mihailescu's Theorem 1 with coprimality added. Then the (p, p, q) family and most signatures are settled, the uniform question is reduced to a small set of exponent triples, and the window's movement is much larger than the number of events suggests. The strongest case for less movement: Sikora's result is a bounded census, not finiteness; both Zhou papers depend on a contested framework and are unrefereed; the Mihailescu statement as extracted is false without coprimality and its date is in conflict; Chocian is 19 days old, with AI credited for much of the work and no review. On the AI question, the strongest case for 'AI was load-bearing' rests on the paper's own statement that Codex was used 'in developing ... mathematical arguments'. The strongest case against rests on the author's statement that he originated the approach and that AI outputs are not certificates.
what_would_settle_it: (a) For Zhou: a referee report or journal acceptance for either paper, an expert statement on whether the argument passes through the Theorem 3.11 to Corollary 3.12 step (the next stage of the LANA project), and the updated version the author promised, to see whether the exception list shrinks. (b) For Mihailescu: a corrected Theorem 1 with coprimality stated, a refereed version, or an expert check of the cyclotomic argument for (p, p, q). (c) For Chocian: expert review of the computations and the inputs, in particular whether Pacetti-Villagra's modularity and conductor results are unconditional, and what the AI tools actually contributed (the Section 8 statement read in full from the PDF). (d) For Sikora: the code and logs, and an independent rerun, plus resolution of the 113 vs 21 range inconsistency. (e) For the uniform question: a theorem covering exponent triples with minimal exponent 2 (the bulk of the known solutions), or a counterexample, neither of which I found.
